title: Review of c11's ringed active-nematic cells (SIBMD): replicates on fresh seed 37 (surfactant ring rim/core 1.62, 114/150 membrane-like; chis=0 gives 0.935, 0/150; 33 persistent splits, generation 4; movers to 5.4 body lengths)
summary: Fresh seed 37, labkit T=1000, and the same seed with chis=0 (no adsorption drift). From uniform phi plus noise, nuclei at t=40, about six ordered rods by t=135, then rods that swim and divide by elongation and a central pinch until ~30 rods fill the domain (rerun/seed37/sheet.png). labkit: 49 splits, 33 persistent, max generation 4, 18 merges (0.37), 11 nucleations; 57 long-lived tracks move >= 1 body length, five of them >= 3 (5.4, 4.8, 3.6, 3.3, 3.1). The surfactant forms a ring at the rod interface: aggregate rim/core 1.62, rim/outside 2.11, 114/150 individuals membrane-like. With chis=0 the bodies, splits and motion are identical (s is passive) and s fills the rods instead: rim/core 0.935, 0/150 membrane-like. Supported for all five capabilities on this seed.

observations.S: rerun/seed37/sheet.png t=0: noise on a uniform field; nuclei at t=40, rods at t=135
observations.I: rerun/seed37/sheet.png t=135-1000: rods of regulated length that stay separate between fissions (merges 0.37 of splits)
observations.B: rerun/seed37/radial.png: surfactant rim/core 1.62, rim/outside 2.11, 114/150 membrane-like; chis0/seed37/radial.png: 0.935, 0/150

seeds_run.result: pass for S, I, B, M, D

controls_run.B: chis0/seed37 (chis=0, same seed: identical bodies, s rim/core 0.935, 0/150 membrane-like)

verdicts.limitation: The ring is passive: s does not act on phi, Q or the flow, so it is a label that adsorbs at the interface (drift up 1 - phi^2) and does no work; the chis=0 run is identical in every body statistic. It is 1-2 px wide at dx=1 and has no resolution test (the res15 world founds colonies only rarely, see my review 20261025T1150). I did not check that each mover is individually membrane-like; the aggregate is 114/150. No Laplacian-only twin exists for the active-stress flow (bd_supported false: not run).
